text:
laura: apiserver spikes in eu-west1, getting a flood of proxy connections and a bunch of controller-manager backlog. GPU-provisioner requests are timing out creating nodes, seeing a bunch of 502/503s to kube-apiserver :eyes:

sre-bot: Incident alert: apiserver_high_connection_count eu-west1 - 2026-03-18T09:21:42Z - lv:critical

jason: checking metrics now — active connections jumped from ~3k to ~23k in <2m. apiserver request latency P99 -> 4.2s. logs show repeated: "proxy: dial tcp x.x.x.x:6443: connect: connection refused" and a few "too many open files" entries

michael: etcd leader is healthy, raft latency okay, but etcd read/write latency has stepped up. also seeing conntrack dropped packets on the nodes (overflow). kube-proxy conntrack counters are in the red on the nodes handling GPU pods

anya: controller-manager backlog is >2000, several reconcile loops for Node/Pod events are timing out. GPU-provisioner webhook calls are hitting 10s timeouts and requeuing. CI/CD burst earlier kicked off ~1500 cluster create ops in eu-west1 — likely the source of the surge

laura: quick mitigation: scaled apiserver deployment +2 replicas in eu-west1 and bumped kube-proxy conntrack max to 200k on the hot AZ. immediate drop in 429s but we need a real root cause. cost alarms triggered though — will revert when stable :grimacing:

jason: here's the quick dump I ran on a problematic node:
```
# conntrack -S
entries: 65535
searched: 987654
drop: 1234
# ss -n | grep 6443 | wc -l
18230
```
looks like we saturated ephemeral conn table and apiserver frontends hit socket limits

michael: long-term fixes: tune kube-proxy conntrack defaults, add admission-side rate limiting on GPU-provisioner, and enforce burst limits for CI jobs. also we should consider adding a small rate-limiter in the control plane path for admission webhooks to avoid head-of-line blocking

anya: I'll push a short-term config change to GPU-provisioner to throttle provisioning: PROVISION_RATE=10/s (canary to eu-west1 first). this should smooth the reconcile storm and reduce controller-manager queue. planning to roll in ~10m

laura: rolling canary now. opened infra ticket INF-3421 for LB/proxy capacity review and conntrack monitoring. tagging @networking and @platform. also adding an alert: controller_manager_queue_length > 500 for >5m

ops-oncall: noted. bumped node conntrack sysctl on the affected pool, will revert after postmortem. please add a runbook entry for emergency conntrack bump. follow-up: add monitoring for apiserver_active_connections and kube-proxy_conntrack_usage

laura: nice triage team. once canary stabilizes we'll de-escalate. creating postmortem stub and assigning owners. :thumbsup:
